parole.significato: Used to form the names of cities and towns, especially in Persian- and Urdu-speaking areas.
parole.testo: From Urdu آباد (-ābād) and Persian ـآباد (-âbâd).

parole.significato: A wedlease (temporary marriage) to a stranger undertaken prior to remarriage to an ex, that is to make the remarriage h…
parole.testo: From Urdu حلالہ (halāla), the practice being called in Eastern Persian حلاله (halâla), while Iranian Persian uses محلل (mohallal), the Arabic term being تَحْلِيل (taḥlīl), scilicet نِكَاح التَحْلِيل (nikāḥ at-taḥlīl), زَوَاج التَحْلِيل (zawāj at-taḥlīl).

parole.significato: A former rank in the British Indian Army, the lowest rank for a viceroy's commissioned officer.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu جمعدار (jamadār), from Persian جمعدار (jam'-dār), from Arabic جَمْع (jamʕ, “gathering”) + Persian ـدار (-dār, “bearer”).

parole.significato: Finely chopped mince as used in South Asia cookery, typically lamb with peas or potatoes and spices, sometimes used as…
parole.testo: From Urdu قیمہ, from Persian قیمه (qime), from Turkic, perhaps Ottoman Turkish قیمه (kıyma), whence Turkish kıyma. Doublet of gheimeh, an Iranian meat stew.

parole.significato: The last couplet of a ghazal, typically incorporating the poet's pen name in a creative way.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu مقطع, from Persian.

parole.significato: A type of enamelwork Persian jewellery, especially champlevé.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu مردہ باد (murda bād, “death to”), from Persian مرده باد (morde bâd).

parole.significato: a person regular in salah; one who goes to the mosque (Islamic equivalent of a parishioner)
parole.testo: From Urdu نَمازی (namāzī), from Urdu نَماز (namāz) and their source, Persian نَمَاز.

parole.significato: The hereditary sovereign of Hyderabad, a former state of India.
parole.testo: From Urdu نظام (nizām) and its source, Persian نظام (nezâm), short for نظام الملک (nezâm el-malek, “a ruler of the realm”).

parole.significato: An Indian rug or mat made with chain stitch.
parole.testo: From Urdu نمدا (namdā), from Persian [script needed] (namad, “carpet”), probably related to Sanskrit नमत (namata, “something woolen”), नवत (navata, “woolen cloth”).
Borrowed from Urdu پاره (pāra), from Persian پاره (pâre).

From Urdu سوار (savār, “swordsman”), borrowed from Persian سوار (savâr, “rider”), from Old Persian 𐎠𐎿𐎲𐎠𐎼 (a-s-b-a-r /⁠asabāra-⁠/, “horseman”), from Proto-Iranian *Hacwabāráh, ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Haćwabʰāras.

parole.significato: An administrative officer in Pakistan and India who gathers taxes from a tehsil.
parole.testo: From Urdu تحصیل دار (taḥṣīl dār), from Persian تحصیلدار, from Arabic تَحْصِيل (taḥṣīl), and Persian دار (dâr).

parole.significato: An Indian landowner who collected local taxes and paid them to the British government.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Urdu زمیندار (zamīndār, “landlord”), from Persian زمیندار.
